mainTopic: Converts from תרמוד, aggadot on enemy nations, and a גוי's קידושין in light of the עשרת השבטים
overview: The גמרא starts with a משנה about stains found among non-Jews. From it, רבי יוחנן learns that converts are accepted even from תרמוד, which clashes with an earlier report in his name. The גמרא answers that different אמוראים reported רבי יוחנן's view in different ways. It then asks why anyone would refuse converts from תרמוד. One view blames the servants of King שלמה. The other blames the men of תרמוד, who attacked the daughters of ירושלים when the היכל was conquered. Next come teachings of רבי יונתן on פסוקים: that שר העולם said 'נער הייתי גם זקנתי', and that עמון and מואב burned the ספרי תורה. Finally, רב אסי rules that a גוי's קידושין today may count, since he might come from the עשרת השבטים. The גמרא limits this to the places where the שבטים settled and begins naming those places, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A משנה shows converts from תרמוד are accepted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about stains teaches that stains from 'among the gentiles' are pure, even in תרמוד. רבי יוחנן learns from this that converts are accepted from תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא ended his teaching with 'from among the gentiles,' and that includes even תרמוד. And רבי יוחנן said: this tells us that we accept converts from תרמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and a statement of רבי יוחנן. Together they show that converts from תרמוד are accepted, which clashes with the earlier view that they are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא reported in רבי יוחנן's name that converts are not accepted from תרמוד. Here רבי יוחנן himself reads the משנה as saying the opposite. So we now have two conflicting statements from the same אמורא.

keyTerms.meaning: He concluded and taught, meaning the תנא finished with a general statement
From among the non-Jews
Tarmod, a city whose people's lineage was suspect
This is to say, a phrase that draws a conclusion from a source
We accept converts

phrases.english: He concluded and taught:
'from among the gentiles,'
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה about stains: stains found in places where non-Jews live are pure.

phrases.english: and even from Tarmod.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is to say, we accept converts from Tarmod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier statement, before this section, that converts from תרמוד are not accepted
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier view in רבי יוחנן's name that converts are not accepted from תרמוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself learns from the משנה that converts from תרמוד are accepted, so the two statements contradict each other

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that רבי יוחנן only reported the inference
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say רבי יוחנן only explained what the משנה implies without agreeing with it. The גמרא rejects this, because רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה always follows a סתם משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that 'this' only means 'this is what the משנה implies,' but he himself does not hold that way, that cannot be. Didn't רבי יוחנן say that the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way out of the contradiction and immediately shuts it down. This makes the contradiction even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way out was: 'זאת אומרת' just describes what the משנה means, not what רבי יוחנן personally holds. But this משנה has no named author, so it is a סתם משנה. רבי יוחנן's own rule is that the הלכה follows such a משנה, so he must agree with it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, introducing a possible answer
He does not hold that way
The halacha follows an unattributed משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack. The גמרא is closing off one possible answer, so the original contradiction from Step 1 still stands.

phrases.english: And if you say 'this' (only reports the implication),
but he himself does not hold so —
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed Mishnah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to the contradiction raised in Step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן only reported the inference without agreeing with it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן rules that the halacha follows a סתם משנה, so he must agree with this one

steps.title: Two versions of רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that different אמוראים disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are אמוראים, and they argue about what רבי יוחנן's opinion was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי יוחנן did not say two opposite things; his students reported his view in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One group of אמוראים said in רבי יוחנן's name that converts from תרמוד are rejected. Another group said in his name that they are accepted. So the conflict is between the people reporting his view, not inside רבי יוחנן himself.

keyTerms.meaning: They are אמוראים, meaning different scholars disagree
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: When one sage seems to contradict himself, the גמרא may answer that his students reported his view differently: 'אמוראי נינהו ואליבא ד...'.

phrases.english: They are amoraim,
and (they argue) according to Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Steps 1 and 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the same sage's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן personally said both that converts from תרמוד are rejected and that they are accepted
steps.terutzMaskana: Different אמוראים reported רבי יוחנן's opinion differently

steps.title: Why not accept converts from תרמוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view that converts from תרמוד are not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: From תרמוד, what is the reason we do not accept converts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants to know what the problem with the people of תרמוד is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually any non-Jew may convert. Refusing a whole town suggests a worry about their lineage, and the גמרא wants to know exactly what that worry is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: From Tarmod, what is the reason (we do) not (accept converts)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether converts are rejected to why they are rejected
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason converts from תרמוד are not accepted

steps.title: Two reasons: שלמה's servants or the daughters of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and the סבייא disagree about the reason. One says it is because of the servants of King שלמה, and the other says it is because of the daughters of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and the elders argue about this. One said: it is because of the servants of שלמה. The other said: it is because of the daughters of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different explanations for the worry about תרמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that there is a lineage problem in תרמוד that could make its people ממזרים. They disagree about where the problem came from: King שלמה's servants, or Jewish women of ירושלים who were taken captive.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders, meaning older sages
The servants of King שלמה
The daughters of ירושלים
One said

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and the elders disagree about it,
one said: because of the servants of Solomon,
and one said: because of the daughters of Jerusalem.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern comes either from King שלמה's servants or from the daughters of ירושלים

steps.title: The servants reason is clear, but what about the daughters reason?
steps.stepSummary: The servants reason works if a child born to a non-Jew or a slave and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. The גמרא then asks what the daughters of ירושלים reason means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who said it is because of שלמה's servants: he holds that if a non-Jew or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר. But for the one who said it is because of the daughters of ירושלים, what is his point?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first reason and then asks what the second reason means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason depends on the view that a child of a non-Jew or a slave with a Jewish woman is a ממזר. That would make the descendants of שלמה's servants ממזרים. The second reason is unclear, especially why it would apply to תרמוד in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense, a setup before 'but'

keyTerms.term: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman
A child of a forbidden union, who may not marry into the community
What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם עַבְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה,
phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said because of the servants of Solomon,

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: he holds: a gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: But according to the one who said because of the daughters of Jerusalem,
what is it?
phrases.notes: He is asking what this reason means, and why it would apply to תרמוד more than anywhere else.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם עַבְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks more closely at the two reasons given in Step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the daughters of ירושלים reason means and why it applies to תרמוד

steps.title: רב יוסף and רבנן disagree about it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף and רבנן disagree about how to explain the daughters reason. Both quote רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף and רבנן argue about this, and both say their view in the name of רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא introduces the people who will explain the daughters reason, and their actual explanations come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No explanation is given yet. We only learn that two parties disagree and that both claim to be quoting the same teacher, רבה בר בר חנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
In the name of

phrases.english: Rav Yosef and the Rabbis disagree about it,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה.
phrases.english: and both of them (speak) in the name of Rabba bar bar Chana.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 6 by introducing a dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The explanation is disputed between רב יוסף and רבנן, both quoting רבה בר בר חנה; the details follow

steps.title: How many soldiers came from תרמוד
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions quoting רבה בר בר חנה disagree about the size of the army from תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said there were twelve thousand men plus six thousand archers. The other said there were twelve thousand men, and six thousand of them were archers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the disagreement between רב יוסף and רבנן from step 7. They argue over how many soldiers from תרמוד took part in the attack on ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides tell the same story. They only argue about the numbers: one says 18,000 in total (12,000 men plus 6,000 archers), and the other says 12,000 in total, with 6,000 of them archers. Either way, a large group from תרמוד was involved, which sets up the story that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish city whose converts are not accepted, according to this view
Twelve
Men (soldiers)
Archers

phrases.english: One said: twelve thousand men
and six thousand archers,
phrases.notes: In this version the archers are on top of the twelve thousand, so 18,000 in all.

phrases.english: and one said: twelve thousand men,
and of them, six thousand archers,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in what the disagreement mentioned in step 7 actually was.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions differ only on the number of soldiers: 12,000 plus 6,000 archers, or 12,000 including 6,000 archers.

steps.title: The men of תרמוד attacked the daughters of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: While everyone else looted the silver and gold of the היכל, the men of תרמוד violated the daughters of ירושלים, as the פסוק in איכה describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the non-Jews entered the היכל, everyone turned to the silver and gold, but they turned to the daughters of ירושלים, as it says: 'They violated women in ציון, young girls in the cities of יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא finally explains the 'daughters of ירושלים' reason from step 5. The men of תרמוד violated Jewish women when the היכל was conquered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from step 6. Because the men of תרמוד fathered children with Jewish women, the view that such a child is a ממזר would treat their descendants as possible ממזרים, so converts from תרמוד are not accepted. The פסוק from איכה serves as the source showing that this really happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary in the בית המקדש
Turned to, went after
The daughters (women) of ירושלים
Violated, abused

steps.whatToRemember: The 'daughters of ירושלים' reason means the men of תרמוד fathered children with Jewish women. Under the view that such children are ממזרים, the people of תרמוד may have ממזר ancestry, so their converts are not accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the explanation of why converts from תרמוד are turned away. It answers the question in step 6 about what the daughters reason means, and, like the servants reason, it depends on the view that a child born to a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

phrases.english: When the non-Jews entered the Sanctuary,
everyone turned to the silver and gold,
but they turned to the daughters of Jerusalem,
as it says: 'They violated women in Zion,'
'young girls in the cities of Judah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the shared story that both versions of step 8 agree on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The men of תרמוד violated the daughters of ירושלים when the היכל was conquered, as the פסוק in איכה describes.

steps.title: The angel over the world said 'I was young and now am old'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says in the name of רבי יונתן that the פסוק 'נער הייתי גם זקנתי' was said by שר העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: This פסוק was said by the angel in charge of the world: 'I was young, and I have also grown old.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about a פסוק from תהלים that was quoted earlier on the daf. רבי יונתן says the speaker of this פסוק is the angel appointed over the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is surprising, since we would expect דוד, the author of תהלים, to be the speaker. The next steps show why the גמרא needs this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel appointed over the world
A verse

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
This verse, the angel over the world said it:
'I was young, and I have also grown old.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:25. This פסוק was quoted earlier on the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching about a פסוק cited earlier on the daf. It does not continue the תרמוד discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The speaker of 'נער הייתי גם זקנתי' is שר העולם.

steps.title: Neither הקב״ה nor דוד fits as the speaker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who could have said the פסוק and rules out both הקב״ה and דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who said it? If you say הקב״ה said it, is there old age before Him? And if דוד said it, was he really that old?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the speaker of the פסוק is and tests the two obvious choices. Both are ruled out, which sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקב״ה does not grow old, so He cannot say 'I have grown old.' דוד did not live long enough to have seen all of history, so 'I was young and now am old' would mean very little coming from him. Removing both choices leaves room for רבי יונתן's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the first suggested answer)
The Holy One, Blessed be He
Old age
Old

phrases.english: Who said it?
If you say the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is there old age before Him?
Rather, David said it?
Was he so very old?
phrases.notes: דוד lived only to seventy, which is not enough to have seen everything this פסוק describes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves step 10 by ruling out the other possible speakers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the speaker of 'נער הייתי גם זקנתי'?

steps.title: So the angel over the world said it
steps.stepSummary: Since neither הקב״ה nor דוד fits, the speaker must be שר העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the angel over the world said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יונתן was right: the speaker is the angel in charge of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel can speak about youth and old age, and he has watched the whole world from its beginning. That makes him the only speaker who fits both parts of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion formula)

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the angel over the world said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the process of elimination from step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'נער הייתי גם זקנתי' was said by שר העולם.

steps.title: עמון and מואב burned the ספרי תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains a פסוק in איכה as referring to עמון ומואב, who burned the ספרי תורה because of the פסוק that keeps them out of the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני also said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the פסוק 'The enemy spread out his hand on all her treasures' mean? This is עמון and מואב. When the non-Jews entered the היכל, everyone went for the silver and gold, but they went for the ספרי תורה. They said: 'This one, which says an Ammonite and a Moabite may not enter the קהל of ה׳, should be burned!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same רבי יונתן. It explains who the 'enemy' in a פסוק from איכה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story follows the same pattern as step 9: everyone else grabbed the silver and gold, but one group went after something else. עמון ומואב went after the ספרי תורה out of hatred for the law that keeps them from marrying into the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק mean? (opens an explanation of a verse)
Her treasures, her precious things
Two nations whose men may not marry into the Jewish people
Torah scrolls
The congregation of ה׳ (marrying into the Jewish people)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'The enemy spread out his hand on all her treasures'?
This is Ammon and Moab.
When the non-Jews entered the Sanctuary,
everyone turned to the silver and gold,
but they turned to the Torah scrolls.
They said: This one, in which is written
'An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord'
should be burned in fire!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by the same speaker. Its story follows the same pattern as the daughters of ירושלים story in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The enemy' in איכה 1:10 refers to עמון ומואב, who burned the ספרי תורה.

steps.title: Hostile neighbors right next to the Jews
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'ה׳ commanded that יעקב's neighbors be his enemies,' רב gives the example of הומניא and פום נהרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ה׳ commanded against יעקב that those around him be his enemies.' רב said: for example, הומניא next to פום נהרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another פסוק from איכה about enemies who live around ישראל. רב gives a real example from his own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ישראל's enemies are its close neighbors. רב points to two neighboring towns, where the people of הומניא troubled the Jews of פום נהרא, as a living example of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Those around him are his enemies
For example
A town whose people were hostile to the Jews
A Jewish town in בבל

phrases.english: 'The Lord commanded against Jacob that those around him be his enemies.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כְּגוֹן הוּמַנְיָא לְפוּם נַהֲרָא.
phrases.english: Rav said: For example, Homanya to Pum Nahara.
phrases.notes: These are two neighboring towns. The people of הומניא made trouble for the Jews of פום נהרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: צִוָּה ה׳ לְיַעֲקֹב סְבִיבָיו צָרָיו, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of enemy nations from step 13 with another פסוק from איכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק's 'neighbors who are enemies' can be seen in הומניא and פום נהרא.

steps.title: A gentile's betrothal today may count
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב אסי: when a גוי does קידושין nowadays, we worry the קידושין are valid, because he may come from the עשרת השבטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב אסי said: If a גוי betroths a woman nowadays, we have to worry that the betrothal counts, because maybe he comes from the ten tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. A new rule is stated: a גוי's קידושין today cannot simply be ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גוי's קידושין mean nothing. But the עשרת השבטים were exiled and mixed in with the nations. So this particular גוי might really be Jewish by descent, and then his קידושין would work.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
Betrothal, the first stage of Jewish marriage
We are concerned; we must take the possibility seriously
The ten tribes of the northern kingdom that were exiled and scattered
Nowadays, in our times

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי does not say the גוי is Jewish. He only says there is a doubt, so we cannot treat the קידושין as nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the קידושין might be valid, the woman could need a גט before marrying someone else.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
A gentile who betrothed [a Jewish woman] nowadays —
we are concerned about the betrothal,
perhaps he is from the ten tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the אגדה about the neighbors of the Jewish people in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי's קידושין today need to be treated as possibly valid, since he may descend from the עשרת השבטים.

steps.title: Anyone who separates is treated like the majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אסי: by the rule of כל דפריש מרובא פריש, any single גוי should be treated as part of the majority, who are real non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: But anyone who comes away from a group is treated as coming from the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אסי's worry. It uses a well-known rule to argue there is no reason to worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of כל דפריש מרובא פריש says that when one person or item leaves a mixed group, we assume it belongs to the majority. Most גוים are not from the עשרת השבטים. So this גוי should be treated as a plain non-Jew, and his קידושין should mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever separates from a group is assumed to come from the majority
But surely; it opens a challenge
The majority

phrases.english: But surely, anything that separates —
separates from the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the worry stated in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's worry about a גוי's קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the majority, any single גוי is assumed to be a real non-Jew, so there is nothing to worry about.

steps.title: The worry is only about where the tribes settled
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the worry applies only in the places where the עשרת השבטים were fixed and settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The worry is about the place where they are settled for good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. It limits his rule to certain places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of כל דפריש only works when someone has left a group. In the places where the שבטים live as a settled group, we are not dealing with someone who left a crowd, so we cannot just follow the majority. There the doubt stays, so the worry about the קידושין is back.

keyTerms.meaning: A place
They are fixed, settled permanently in one place

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the majority rule is wrong. It only says the rule does not apply to people found in their fixed place.

phrases.english: [It is said] about the place where they are fixed.
phrases.notes: "They" means the ten tribes, in the places where they were settled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by narrowing step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי's worry seemed to cover every גוי anywhere, so following the majority should have cancelled it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry applies only to people from the places where the שבטים are settled, where we cannot follow the majority.

steps.title: A verse lists where the ten tribes were placed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אבא בר כהנא, who reads a פסוק listing the places where the exiled tribes were settled and identifies each place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבא בר כהנא said: "And he placed them in חלח and in חבור, by the river of גוזן, and in the cities of מדי." חלח is חלזון. And חבור is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer by showing which places the שבטים were settled in. It starts listing them, and the list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 17 needs to know which places count as where the שבטים are settled. רבי אבא בר כהנא takes the places named in the פסוק and gives the names they had in his own day. On this amud we only see חלח, which is חלזון, before the list goes on to חבור on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And he placed them, settled them
Halah, one of the places of the exile
Habor, another place of the exile
The cities of Media

and Habor:
